items.title: Raíz y Barrio
items.technique: Spray paint and acrylic on wall
items.description: Large-format mural honoring Paraguayan urban biodiversity. Inspired by naturalist Moisés Bertoni. Features 17 real residents of Barrio Mariscal in everyday scenes, integrating native plant species.

items.title: Dead Sea
items.description: Dynamic map of the shrinking Dead Sea. Deep blue where water remains, red where desert has taken over. Created for Artists 4 Israel for Earth Day 2023.

items.title: Ghost Organ
items.description: Solo exhibition at Arte Actual gallery. Plastic pieces exploring abstract sensations through illustration processes. A visual investigation of what is no longer there but still resonates.

items.title: Oliva & Ayolas Mural
items.location: Oliva c/ Ayolas y O'Leary, Downtown Asunción
items.description: Iconic mural in downtown Asunción, designed to visually refresh the city center. An urban intervention transforming a downtown building into an artistic landmark.

items.title: Nescafé Limited Edition Cans
items.description: Three limited edition can designs for Nescafé, inspired by everyday Paraguayan life. A collaboration that brought urban art to supermarket shelves nationwide.

items.title: Sinvergüenzas
items.description: First intervention in Buenos Aires, alongside Argentine artist Ice. A group exhibition marking the beginning of his international projection.

items.title: Twisted Sky
items.description: A mural that plays with perspective and the Paraguayan urban landscape. A distorted sky folds over itself, questioning the relationship between the natural and the built in the metropolitan area of Asunción.

items.title: Seeds in the Air
items.description: Series of illustrations about the dispersion of native Paraguayan seeds. Combines botany and urban art, published as an editorial series and exhibited at Espacio Concentra gallery.

items.title: Visor
items.description: Cover and interior illustrations for the graphic novel 'Visor'. A work that fuses Oz's urban style with sequential narrative, exploring Paraguayan identity through comics.

items.title: Downtown Guide
items.description: Collaborative mural in downtown Asunción that functions as a visual guide to the neighborhood. Points to cultural, historical and commercial landmarks through graphic language combining maps, popular iconography and lettering.

items.title: Estudio 8 Murals
items.description: Series of corporate murals created through Estudio 8 for Paraguayan brands and commercial spaces. Turnkey projects including branding, concept design, execution and professional documentation.

items.title: Southern Biennial
items.description: Participation in the Southern Biennial with a mural addressing South American identity from an urban art perspective. A visual reflection on what it means to be from the south, far from hegemonic art centers.

items.title: Electric Roots
items.description: Piece from the 'Electric Roots' series exploring the tension between tradition and modernity in Paraguay. Acrylic, aerosol and digital collage on canvas. Part of a private collection.

items.title: Powerline Facade
items.description: Facade mural of Powerline Shop, Paraguay's first graffiti and urban art store. A visual icon that marked a milestone for the local scene and remains a meeting point for Asunción's urban art community.

biografia.title: About
biografia.intro: Oscar Saúl Montanía Villar (Asunción, 1985), known as Oz Montanía, is one of Paraguay's most influential urban artists, illustrators and graphic designers, and a key reference for street art in Latin America. With over two decades of work, he has transformed Asunción's urban landscape and taken his art to cities around the world.

timeline.detail: Grows up in Fernando de la Mora. His parents run a small book distribution business, sparking his love for reading and illustrations from early childhood.
Sees the first punk graffiti in his neighborhood. At 10, picks up a spray can for the first time and paints his own house wall. 'Obviously the worst idea,' he recalls.
Inspired by skate and punk culture, starts painting on the street with tags. His first recognizable drawing: Bart Simpson.
Paints his first mural at 17. Leaves home and becomes self-sufficient.
Attends Graphic Design at Universidad Católica de Asunción. Works by day as editorial illustrator, graphic creative and art director.
Travels to Buenos Aires and paints with Argentine artist Ice at the Sinvergüenzas show at the Spain Cultural Center. A turning point in his technique.
Creates Estudio 8, his design and art production studio, coordinating large-format murals and commercial projects.
Paraguay's first specialized graffiti and urban art supply store. A milestone for the local scene which previously lacked access to materials.
Travels to the West Bank invited by Artists 4 Israel to paint a mural about the Dead Sea's disappearance. A dynamic map showing the retreat of the saltiest sea on Earth.
Solo exhibition at Arte Actual gallery in Asunción. Also designs the limited edition Nescafé cans.
Inaugurates his most ambitious mural at Shopping Mariscal: 30 meters wide honoring urban biodiversity, featuring 17 real neighborhood residents. Curated by Laura Mandelik.
Oz remains active with commissioned murals, international collaborations and his role as a reference for Paraguayan urban art.

biografia.quote: In any of those categories, you generate images. That can be the starting point: someone who makes images. I hope this craft takes me to create things beyond that.

section_influencias.title: Influences
section_influencias.text: Comics (DC, Marvel, Image, manga), classic engraving (Gustave Doré, Albrecht Dürer), punk, 90s pop culture, Guaraní mythology, Paraguayan biodiversity, and a voracious curiosity for music, film and animation.

section_filosofia.title: Philosophy
section_filosofia.text: Oz believes art must take a stand on human rights and environmental issues, represent those historically without a voice, and be built from the honesty of craft rather than market labels.

items.title: How I made Raíz y Barrio
items.excerpt: The process behind the largest mural I've painted to date: 30 meters wide, 17 real neighbors portrayed, and a tribute to Paraguayan biodiversity.
items.content: Raíz y Barrio was a challenge unlike anything I had done before. Not just because of the size — 30 meters wide by 8 meters tall — but because of what it represented: the first time portraying real people from the neighborhood in a mural...

items.title: Painting the Dead Sea
items.excerpt: A journey to the West Bank to paint a mural about the Dead Sea environmental crisis, invited by Artists 4 Israel for Earth Day.
items.content: When I received the invitation from Artists 4 Israel to paint in the West Bank, I knew I had to do something that truly communicated the urgency of the problem...

items.title: Powerline Shop: Paraguay's first graffiti store
items.excerpt: How the idea of opening Paraguay's first specialized graffiti and urban art supply store came to be.
items.content: Before Powerline, getting a quality spray can in Paraguay was an odyssey. You had to bring them from Argentina or Brazil, or settle for what was available...
